html:
NATO, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, is a military alliance of North American and European states, founded by treaty in Washington on 4 April 1949. Its heart is Article 5: an armed attack on one member counts as an attack on all.

Twelve states founded it, led by the United States, to deter the Soviet Union in the Cold War. Turkey and Greece joined in 1952 and West Germany in 1955, which led the Soviets to set up the rival Warsaw Pact that year. Iceland had no army but gave the alliance a key air base, which it used as leverage in the Cod Wars with Britain.

After the Soviet Union fell in 1991, NATO took in former communist states:

  • Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic in 1999.
  • Seven more in 2004, among them Slovakia, Slovenia and the three Baltic states.

It fought its first wars in the Balkans, bombing in Bosnia in 1995 and Kosovo in 1999. Article 5 was invoked only once, after the attacks on the United States in September 2001, and NATO then kept forces in Afghanistan until 2021. Russia saw its growth as a threat. After Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, Finland and Sweden gave up long neutrality and joined, bringing it to 32 members.
sum: NATO, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, is a military alliance of North American and European states, founded by treaty in Washington on 4 April 1949. Its heart is Article 5: an armed attack on one member counts as an attack on all.
